title: Pavers spreading at the edges? Edge restraint

A.note: band at 1.18-1.20x effective, bottom-left of the photo (x 0-914, y 204-878): the hi-vis worker on the deck and the blue marker flag in the lawn are both outside the crop

B.note: band at 1.16-1.18x effective showing photo x 0-929: the bins and the house at the right edge are outside the crop; the two hi-vis workers at the back fence stay small and unidentifiable

headline: GAPS OPENING
AT THE *EDGES?*
beats.vo: Pavers spreading at the edges? Check what's holding the edge.

headline: NO RESTRAINT?
THEY *CREEP*
beats.vo: Every paver edge that isn't against a curb or wall needs an *edge restraint*, or the pavers slowly *creep* apart.

headline: BASE RUNS
*PAST* THE EDGE
beats.vo: The base runs *past* the restraint, as far as the base is thick. *Six inch* base, *six inches* past.

headline: HIDDEN UNDER
THE *LAWN EDGE*
beats.vo: Once the lawn or mulch goes in, you *never see it*. That's the point.

beats.prompt: SEND THIS TO A PATIO OWNER
beats.vo: Send this to a patio owner.

post.caption: Paver edges spreading on your Lower Mainland patio? Every paver edge that isn't against a curb or wall needs an edge restraint, with the compacted base running past it by at least the base thickness. On a finished job it's hidden under the lawn or mulch.
post.alt: A paver pool deck meeting a lawn in a clean curve, and an animated cross-section of an edge restraint holding the outer pavers in place.
